tasks.short: Document technical specifications and operating standards

steps.what: Submit equipment id and operating limits

loop.input: equipment form and the current standard
loop.output: gap list of missing or conflicting limits
loop.check: Each gap names an equipment id that is on the form
loop.stop: One pass, then the specialist finishes any row with no equipment id
loop.why_not_simpler: Old prose limits do not match equipment ids by a fixed rule

steps.what: Draft technical specifications from the fields

loop.output: specification draft with each limit tagged to a field
loop.check: Every operating limit and equipment id equals the submitted field
loop.stop: Leave a blank and stop that section if a limit has no field
loop.why_not_simpler: How a limit is worded still varies by equipment type

tasks.design: Service owners submit equipment id, site, operating limit, version and owner on a {WORKFLOW} form. A bounded draft fills the specification template in {DOCS} from those fields only. Metadata columns for equipment id, version and owner may be filled from the form, and the specialist checks them because a fill can be wrong. The specialist signs one version of the operating standard.
tasks.previous_blocker: Operating limits lived in old documents and mail, so a generated draft would have copied a stale equipment id.
tasks.enabler_now: The equipment record and the form can share one equipment id, so each limit in the draft can be checked against a field.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding the operating limit for a live service is still a judgement, not a merge of fields.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist decides which limit is safe and which old sentence must not be copied forward.

ambition.what: Re-sign the operating standard when the equipment changes, not only at the yearly review

tasks.altitude: The week moves from rewriting sections to conflicts and the signature. The specialist can refuse a standard whose equipment id or limit does not match the form.

reach.task: Design a change against the signed operating standard
reach.learn: Which equipment has a signed standard and which limits are still blank

evidence.claim: In a mid-size firm this task is mostly a specification document plus a review. The hard part is the operating limit, not the layout.
Digest [S3] says a document product can fill metadata from a prompt, and the vendor warns the fill can be wrong. Use that only for equipment id, version and owner, not for the specification body.

assumptions: Focal role is the telecommunications specialist. The task ends when a signed standard version is filed. Configuring the equipment is a later task.

Input contract: equipment id, site, operating limit, version, owner. Producer is the service owner. If the form is empty the specialist types the same fields from the old document and marks the row manual.
Use the document store's own templates and approval flow before custom code. The meeting prior overstates this task: most time is the document, and the sign-off is a review of one version.
unknowns: Which store holds the current operating standard.
Who may sign when the specialist is absent.
Whether old scanned standards have an equipment id at all.
research_questions: How often does a signed limit differ from the equipment actually in service?
Which equipment types have no named owner?

already_counted.description: Specialist edits weak operating-limit sections in the draft
Specialist resolves conflicting limits in the sign-off

incremental.description: Update the specification template when a new equipment type appears
Service owners correct limits the form rejects

approvals.approved_version: operating standard version signed in this review
the same signed operating standard version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes half the equipment still arrives as free text, so the specialist retypes limits. The high case assumes the form is used but every standard still has a full sign-off. Configuring the live equipment is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Diagnose device problems and apply a reviewed fix

steps.what: Report the network and device problems
Diagnose network and device problems with the user

loop.input: symptom text and existing knowledge notes
loop.output: a procedural note that cites one note id
loop.check: The cited note id exists and matches the confirmed category
loop.stop: If no note matches, return an empty draft and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: A new symptom phrase does not match a note by a fixed table

steps.what: Sign the support fix for this ticket
Apply the technical or procedural fix

tasks.design: The system user opens a ticket on {HELPDESK} with device id, site and symptom. The desk suggests a category and drafts a knowledge note for the specialist to review. The diagnosis conversation stays with the specialist and the user. A known procedural note can be sent after review. A technical change on the device stays with the specialist and is never left unattended.
tasks.previous_blocker: Symptoms arrived as free text in mail and calls, so similar device problems did not line up with a knowledge note.
tasks.enabler_now: The desk can suggest a category from the symptom text, and a device id can key a reviewed note.
tasks.still_hard: A fault that does not match a note, and any live change on the device, still depends on the conversation and the specialist's hands.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist decides whether the user is describing a known fault and whether a live change is safe.

ambition.what: Staff at sites with no resident specialist get a reviewed procedural note before anyone travels

tasks.altitude: Known faults take less searching. The specialist keeps the diagnosis conversation and the right to refuse a live change.

reach.task: Confirm the device works after the fix
reach.learn: Which symptoms already have a reviewed note and which still need a person

evidence.claim: In a mid-size firm, user support for network and device problems is a conversation plus a change. Only repeated symptoms suit a reviewed note.
Digest [S1] and [S2] say a service desk can suggest a ticket category and draft a knowledge item for a person to review. That fits user support, not design work.
Digest [S15] is a vendor self-service claim of fewer tickets, with no published baseline, so it is not treated as a measured saving. It applies only to user support.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so an unattended change on live telecommunications equipment is out of scope.

assumptions: Focal role is the telecommunications specialist. The task runs from a user report to a confirmed device or a stopped attempt.
Input contract: device id, site, symptom text, ticket id, contact. Producer is the system user. Tickets with no device id stay on the manual diagnosis queue.

Use the helpdesk's own categories and knowledge draft before custom code. The high meeting prior is accepted: the diagnosis is a conversation, not console work. Logging stays the ticket, not a record of how the user spoke.
unknowns: Which devices the specialist can change remotely.
Whether the knowledge note is visible to all staff or only to the desk.
research_questions: What share of device problems repeat a symptom already in a reviewed note?
How often does the first technical fix get rolled back?

already_counted.description: Specialist edits a weak procedural note before signing
Diagnosis conversation stays with the specialist
Hands-on technical fix stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Retire knowledge notes that no longer match the equipment
Users resubmit tickets that lack a device id

approvals.approved_version: support fix signed for this ticket id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most symptoms have no matching note, so the specialist still diagnoses by conversation. The high case assumes known faults draft cleanly but every diagnosis and every live change stays manual. No unattended changes, and the vendor ticket claim is not counted as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Accept a renovation done with vendors

steps.what: Draft the renovation brief from the record

loop.input: project fields and the brief template
loop.output: brief that cites the site id and milestone id
loop.check: Site id and milestone id equal the project record
loop.stop: Stop the section if the site id is missing
loop.why_not_simpler: Vendor scope prose does not fit a fixed sentence

steps.what: Vendor engineers complete the renovation work
Walk the renovation and accept or reject it

tasks.design: A {PROJECT} record holds site, scope, vendor and milestone. The specialist drafts a short renovation brief in {DOCS} from those fields. Vendor engineers and installers do the physical work. The specialist accepts the site only after a walkthrough. No live cutover runs unattended.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scope and vendor promises lived in mail threads, so a brief could not show which milestone it belonged to.
tasks.enabler_now: The project record can carry a site id, a vendor name and a milestone id on one row.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the installed work matches the building, and whether to accept it, is still a walkthrough.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist accepts or rejects the renovation and names what the vendor must still fix.

ambition.what: Accept or reject each renovation milestone when the site changes, not only at a final meeting

tasks.altitude: Less time rewriting the brief, same time on the site with vendors. The specialist can refuse a handover that has no walkthrough.

reach.task: Finish the open items from the handover
reach.learn: Which milestone was accepted and which items are still open

evidence.claim: Renovation work in a mid-size firm is mostly coordination with installers and vendors, plus a site walk. The brief is the small part.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so an unattended cutover on live telecommunications equipment is out of scope.

assumptions: Focal role is the telecommunications specialist. The task ends at an accepted or rejected handover. The vendor's build method is not redesigned here.
Input contract: site id, scope text, vendor name, milestone id, planned date. Producer is the service owner. Rows with no site id are not briefed and stay in mail.
Use the project record's own fields before custom code. The high meeting prior is accepted: vendor work and the walkthrough stay in person.
unknowns: Which milestones the specialist may accept alone.
Whether a landlord controls access to the site.
research_questions: How often is a renovation rejected at the walkthrough?
Which vendors still send scope only as an attachment?

already_counted.description: Specialist edits the brief before it goes to the vendor
Walkthrough and acceptance stay with the specialist

incremental.description: Keep the brief template aligned when a new milestone type appears
Vendors resend completion notes that lack a milestone id

approvals.approved_version: renovation handover signed at this walkthrough

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes the scope still arrives as mail, so the brief is rare and the walkthrough is unchanged. The high case assumes the brief is clean but every vendor visit and every acceptance stays manual. The physical install is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Note industry changes from literature and workshops

steps.what: Talk with colleagues about industry changes

loop.output: note that cites one title and one practice
loop.check: Each cited title is on the reading list
loop.stop: One draft, then drop any sentence with no title
loop.why_not_simpler: Why a practice matters here is not a lookup on the title

steps.what: Accept the change note for filing

tasks.design: A reading list in {DOCS} holds title, source and date for current literature. The specialist still talks with colleagues and still attends the workshop, meeting or conference. A bounded note records which telecommunications practice changed. The network architect can read that note. Attendance itself is not a system record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Literature and workshop takeaways were private notes, so a later project could not see what the specialist had already judged relevant.
tasks.enabler_now: Titles and dates can sit on one list, and a note can cite a title instead of pasting the whole article.
tasks.still_hard: Judging which emerging practice matters here, and being in the room, does not become a feed.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist decides which change is worth a note and which is noise.

ambition.what: File a short change note after each workshop, not only when a project asks

tasks.altitude: Less time hunting for the article afterwards. Conferences and colleague conversations stay as they are. The specialist can ignore a change that does not affect this network.

reach.task: Decide whether a noted practice changes a current design
reach.learn: Which practices the specialist has already marked as relevant and when

evidence.claim: Keeping up with telecommunications practice is reading plus conversations and events. A note can be filed. The event cannot be skipped.
A title and date list is ordinary document work. It does not judge whether a practice should change this firm's network.

assumptions: Focal role is the telecommunications specialist. The task ends when a change note is filed or the specialist decides not to file one. It does not include buying a product.
Input contract: title, source, date, practice name. Producer is the specialist from the literature at hand. Items with no source stay off the list.
Use the document list and the calendar as they are before custom code. The meeting prior is accepted for workshops and conferences. Colleague talk is not treated as already written down.
unknowns: Which events the specialist is expected to attend.
Whether the change note is shared outside the technology team.
research_questions: How many literature items become a filed note in a typical month?
Which notes later changed an operating standard?

already_counted.description: Colleague conversations stay with the specialist
Workshop and conference time stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Retire reading-list rows that no longer have a source

approvals.approved_version: change note accepted in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes almost every item is still a private note, so only the list is new. The high case assumes notes are filed but every workshop, meeting and colleague conversation stays manual. Reading time is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The specialist stops retyping standards and chasing every article, and spends the week on device faults that do not match a known fix and on whether a renovation is actually finished.
reach: The network architect receives the signed operating standard instead of an old attachment.
The service owner receives the renovation handover with the accepted site and the open items.
skills_to_grow: Write an operating standard as fields a template can check.
Separate a known device fault from a live change on the equipment.
Keep a short note from a workshop instead of rewriting the whole standard.
role.ambitious_version: Every equipment type has a signed operating standard, and a known device fault can close from a reviewed desk note without a site visit.
